title: The on-chain deploy workflow runs a user-supplied command, and dry-run provably does not
expectation: Deployment is execution, not release planning, so it lives in a configured `[cli.deploy]` workflow as a Command step wrapping the workspace's own deploy script (a stand-in for `pina deploy --cluster <rpc> ... --yes`, which wraps `solana program deploy`). `monochange run deploy --dry-run` must exit 0, report the dry-run command, and leave no deploy marker; the real run must execute the script and leave the marker. These mechanical properties are tested without a model and without the Solana toolchain.

checks.command: rm -f .deploy-ran; monochange run deploy --dry-run; rc=$?; test $rc -eq 0 && test ! -f .deploy-ran
checks.why: A deploy dry run must be safe to run anywhere: it prints the command it would run and must not execute the mutating side of the deploy script.

checks.command: monochange run deploy; rc=$?; test $rc -eq 0 && test -f .deploy-ran; rc2=$?; rm -f .deploy-ran; test $rc -eq 0 -a $rc2 -eq 0
checks.why: The real run must execute the configured command exactly once and surface its output, which is the entire execution story for on-chain upgrades today: monochange plans and records, the user's command deploys.
